articles.title: Francesca clapcich is eighth in IMOCA
articles.excerpt: Italian-American skipper Francesca Clapcich brought her IMOCA 11th Hour Racing across the finish line of the 13th edition of the Route du Rhum Destination Guadeloupe at 18:41:09 hrs local time (23:41:09hrs UTC) to take eighth place from a 22 boat fleet which started the 3542 nautical miles solo Atlantic sprint from Saint Malo on Sunday 1st November.

articles.title: Damien Seguin, winner in the Vintage Multi* !
articles.excerpt: His is a triumph with a whiff of legend to it, one that Damien Seguin could reflect on when he crossed the finish line of the Route du Rhum - Destination Guadeloupe this Thursday, November 12, at 4:24:34 PM (local time).

articles.title: Sam Goodchild: fourth is not good enough, but neither is second or third
articles.excerpt:
Sam Goodchild misses IMOCA podium by 11 minutes at the end of challenging Route du Rhum Destination Guadeloupe

 

For Franco-Brit Sam Goodchild, skipper of MACIF Santé Prevoyance, fourth place into Gudeloupe this morning concluded what proved to be a very challenging Route du Rhum Destination Gudeloupe, suffering too many technical problems to be able to operate at close to maximum potential.

articles.title: 📸 EVERY morning, a little closer to Guadeloupe
articles.excerpt: Les jours passent et les skippers encore en mer poursuivent leur route vers la Guadeloupe ! Chaque lever et coucher de soleil offre de magnifiques couleurs sur l’Atlantique, tandis que les milles continuent de défiler. Des instants précieux capturés depuis le bord, au cœur d’une traversée qui réserve encore de belles images !

articles.title: Sam Goodchild (MACIF SANTÉ PrÉvoyance), fourth in the la Route du Rhum-Destination guadeloupe
articles.excerpt: As a favorite in this Route du Rhum—his first in the IMOCA class—Sam Goodchild faced a challenging race between Saint-Malo and Pointe-à-Pitre. Finding himself outsmarted early in the race he watched helplessly as Corentin Horeau (MACSF) pulled miles ahead, and spent the remainder of the race pushing hard to catch up with Boris Herrmann (Malizia 4). A mainsail failure and some foil issues slowed him down while passing through a tropical depression; this opening allowed Elodie Bonafous...

articles.title: Élodie Bonafous (Association Petits Princes Quéguiner) takes third place in the Route du Rhum – Destination Guadeloupe in the IMOCA class
articles.excerpt: Showing typical drive and self confidence right to the finish line, Elodie Bonafous stayed cool under pressure, holding her own against a spirited fightback from Franco-Brit Sam Goodchild (MACIF Santé Prévoyance) to take an excellent third place in the IMOCA class on the Route du Rhm Destination Guadeloupe. articles.title: 🌦️ WEATHER CONSULT BULLETIN OF NOVEMBER 12
articles.excerpt: Ce jeudi 12 novembre, onze jours après le départ de la Route du Rhum – Destination Guadeloupe 2026, Alexia Barrier et Anne-Claire Le Berre marquent l’histoire en devenant les premières femmes à boucler une transatlantique en solitaire, respectivement en Ultim et en Ocean Fifty.

articles.title: Boris herrmann second in imoca on the route du rhum destination guadeloupe
articles.excerpt: Finishing in early morning rain German skipper Boris Herrmann added to his growing list of solo Transatlantic successes today when he took second  place in the IMOCA class on the 13th edition of the Route du Rhum Destination, the solo ocean sprint from Saint Malo to Gudeloupe.

articles.title: Anne-Claire Le Berre (Upwind By Merconcept), seventh in the Route du Rhum – Destination Guadeloupe in the Ocean Fifty class
articles.excerpt: She is the first woman to participate in and complete a solo transatlantic race in the Ocean Fifty class! With a diverse background, Anne-Claire Le Berre has fulfilled a dream by skippering the trimaran for which she was selected by MerConcept to take on the role of a pioneer.

articles.title: Alexia Barrier : “I am hungry to return and do more”
articles.excerpt: Twenty minutes before reaching the finish line she shed tears of joy. Once she crossed it, Alexia Barrier celebrated on the bow of her boat as she ebcame the first woman to complete a transatlantic crossing solo in the  Ultim class on the Route du Rhum Destination Guadeloupe.

articles.title: Armel Le Cléac’h: « I was lucky to have the chance to survive »
articles.excerpt: For the first time, the skipper of the Maxi Banque Populaire XI has opened up about his vessel’s capsize. After arriving in Norfolk, Virginia (USA), Armel Le Cléac’h reunited with his wife, Aurélia Le Cléac’h, and the sports director of Team Banque Populaire. In an extensive video and an official statement, he discusses the capsize and his subsequent rescue in detail, while also looking ahead to what comes next

articles.title: Fiftys shades of gold
articles.excerpt: fter last night’s champagne sprays and tears of joy from winner Basile Bourgnon (Edenred) have dried, three more Ocean Fifty trimarans celebrated their arrival in Pointe-à-Pitre this Wednesday morning. Having successfully completed this Route du Rhum – Destination Guadeloupe, before discussing the competition or even the final standings the skippers all shared their enthusiasm and satisfaction with an exceptional race.

articles.title: hope springs eternal
articles.excerpt:
A one-hour penalty has been issued to Thibaut Vauchel-Camus (Solidaires En Peloton by Delanchy)—currently second in the Ocean Fifty class—following the accidental breakage of an engine seal.

There is still the possibility of surprises as light winds approaching Guadeloupe and around the island are potential traps.

articles.title: 🌦️ WEATHER CONSULT BULLETIN OF NOVEMBER 11
articles.excerpt: Ce mercredi 11 novembre, dix jours après le départ de la Route du Rhum – Destination Guadeloupe 2026, Basile Bourgnon et Corentin Horeau remportent les Ocean Fifty et les IMOCA, à deux minutes d’intervalle à Pointe-à-Pitre. En mer, les vents faibles ralentissent encore une partie des concurrents à l’approche des Antilles. Plus à l’est, un nouveau front concerne certains Class40, avant que la reconstitution progressive de l’anticyclone des Açores ne modifie les conditions de navigation.

articles.title: Bourgnon, Horeau and a wave of emotions
articles.excerpt: Tonight at the Mémorial ACTe, everything came together to sweep the crowd off their feet as they gathered to witness the simultaneous finishes of the winners in the Ocean Fifty and IMOCA classes. There were plenty of stories, shared experiences, and bucket loads of emotion. Both sharing a space on cloud nine, Basile Bourgnon and Corentin Horeau spoke of the magic of the Route du Rhum-Destination Guadeloupe.
